citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 1525–1534.
creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández (CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam)
description: LAMBADA is a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task requiring a broad discourse context. It consists of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word when exposed to the whole passage, but not when only seeing the last sentence.
name: LAMBADA
publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 unsuccessful guesses or 2 successful guesses per item.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human subjects recruited through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: In the crowdsourcing pipeline, 84–86% items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2 and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all the selection steps.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1. one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if the guess was right, 2. a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if that guess was also right, 3. more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10; if no subject was able to guess the target word, the passage was added to the LAMBADA dataset. Subjects in step 3 were allowed 3 guesses per sentence.
rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA (48%), while other categories are under-represented compared to the POS distribution in the input. The dataset also contains (quoted) direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% vs 61%).
rai:dataCollection: Data was sourced from the Book Corpus. Passages were first filtered using four language models to exclude those easily guessable by standard models. The remaining passages were then evaluated by human subjects on CrowdFlower to ensure the missing word could be guessed from the broad context but not from the local sentence context alone.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data comes from the Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), which contains unpublished novels. The corpus contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Passages were filtered using a combination of four language models. Any passage whose target word had probability >=0.00175 according to any of the language models was excluded.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list.
rai:dataUseCases: To evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task, specifically testing their ability to keep track of information in the broader discourse.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A combination of four language models: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) and three models trained on the Book Corpus (a standard 4-gram model, a RNN and a feed-forward model).

null_reasons.rai:dataLimitations: No specific limitations discussed other than the noted bias towards proper nouns.
